A field-facing review arguing that null-model choice, not statistical power,
is the dominant source of false discovery in spatial tissue imaging studies.
Surveys published neighborhood-enrichment analyses and finds that a majority
use a random-labeling null that does not account for large-scale spatial
gradients, which the authors show analytically and by simulation inflates
apparent significance. Proposes spatially-constrained permutation testing as
the field default and recommends segmentation uncertainty be carried through
to any downstream statistical claim rather than discarded after quality
control. Closes with a call for reporting standards that require authors to
state their null-model choice explicitly.
